program_name: DER and Aggregation Participation Model - Energy (LBMP)
incentive_structure: $/MWh Day-Ahead and Real-Time LBMP settled at the Aggregation's Transmission Node; dispatch-only (no start-up/commitment parameters)
event_limits: Min 10 kW per individual DER asset (Services Tariff 4.1.10.1); max Injection Limit 20 MW per facility; six-second real-time telemetry required for each Aggregation plus hourly revenue-quality meter data by noon next business day; Aggregator must be reachable 24x7 for verbal real-time operations; Demand Reductions below the Monthly Net Benefit Threshold are not eligible for energy payments unless dispatched for reliability
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Sections 4.1.10, 4.5.2, 4.5.7, 17; Aggregation Manual Sections 2.2.1, 6.1.10, 6.2
export_compensation: Settled at Transmission Node LBMP; withdrawals by Withdrawal-Eligible Generators treated as negative generation
stackable_with: ICAP market participation (required to also be in Energy market); NOT stackable with SCR or EDRP - a Resource may not simultaneously be a DER in an Aggregation and an SCR/EDRP Resource (Aggregation Manual 4.3.2); dual participation with utility CSRP/DLRP/DLM permitted with notice

program_name: DER and Aggregation Participation Model - Installed Capacity (ICAP) Supplier
incentive_structure: $/kW-month UCAP sold into Strip, Monthly and ICAP Spot Market auctions; UCAP = Aggregation ICAP x Capacity Accreditation Factor x derating factor
event_limits: Aggregation must submit DMNC test data per season; at least one DER in the Aggregation must be participating in the capacity market; ICAP participation requires simultaneous Energy market participation; new ICAP suppliers must run one month in the Energy market first; ICAP Suppliers must bid the ICAP-equivalent of UCAP sold into the Day-Ahead Market every hour (or schedule a bilateral, or notify NYISO of an outage); two-year outage schedule required at enrollment
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Sections 5.12.1.3, 5.12.3, 5.12.7, 5.12.13.1; ICAP Manual Sections 4.2, 4.3, 4.8; ICAP Manual Attachment J Sections 3.0 and 6.9; Aggregation Manual Section 2.2.5
stackable_with: ICAP + Energy + Ancillary Services simultaneously; NOT stackable with SCR (an SCR must separate in DRIS before transitioning; a DER that exits must give notice by Aug 1 and can only rejoin SCR the following May 1)

program_name: DER and Aggregation Participation Model - Ancillary Services (Regulation and Operating Reserves)
incentive_structure: $/MWh market clearing price for Regulation Capacity/Movement and for 10-Minute Spinning, 10-Minute Non-Synchronized, 30-Minute Synchronized and 30-Minute Non-Synchronized Reserves
event_limits: Under current (pre-Order-2222) rules every individual DER in the Aggregation must itself be capable of the service offered - the Aggregation can only offer the lowest-quality product common to all its members (Aggregation Manual 2.2.4); Aggregations providing reserves or regulation must bid self-committed flexible; self-committed fixed and ISO-committed fixed bid modes are ineligible for Operating Reserves; new reserve Aggregations verify performance during the first two weeks of the first active month rather than prequalifying
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Section 15.4.1.2.4 and Rate Schedule 4; Aggregation Manual Section 2.2.4; Ancillary Services Manual Section 6.12.2
stackable_with: Energy + ICAP + Ancillary Services can be provided by the same Aggregation; the all-members-capable restriction is scheduled to change with NYISO's Order 2222 implementation

program_name: Dual Participation - NYISO Aggregation plus utility DR program (CSRP / DLRP / DLM)
incentive_structure: No separate payment - this is the rule permitting a DER to earn both NYISO market revenue and utility DR program revenue
event_limits: PERMITTED. An Aggregation containing DER that also participate in programs meeting distribution-system needs in the NYCA must notify NYISO of dual participation at enrollment (Market Participant User's Guide Section 1.2); the Aggregation's NYISO offers must be constructed so the Aggregation is scheduled by NYISO whenever it operates to meet the non-wholesale commitment (Services Tariff 4.1.11). NYISO confirms CSRP, DLRP and DLM are covered by this categorization. Dual-participation requirements are scheduled to change when NYISO implements its Order 2222-compliant tariff (targeted end of 2026)
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Section 4.1.11; Market Participant User's Guide Section 1.2
stackable_with: Con Edison CSRP; Con Edison DLRP; Joint Utilities Dynamic Load Management (DLM); NOT stackable with NYISO SCR or EDRP

program_name: DER Aggregation - Telemetry and Metering Requirements
incentive_structure: Cost gate, not a revenue stream
event_limits: Six-second real-time telemetry (a meter read every six seconds) required for each Aggregation, plus hourly revenue-quality meter data. Four telemetry channels required regardless of composition: Energy injections, Energy withdrawals, Demand Reductions, and total response MW (zeros for non-applicable channels), plus a point for actual Aggregation load. NYISO sends Base Point Signals to the Aggregation, not to individual DER. End-to-End Communication Testing among Aggregator control center, Member System (TO) and NYISO required for every new Aggregation enrollment; adding a DER to an existing Aggregation does not require re-testing. Meter Authority must be an authorized Meter Services Entity, the municipal utility, or the Member System
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Sections 4.1.10.4, 13, 13.3.2, 13.3.2.1; Aggregation Manual Section 7.3; Revenue Metering Requirements Manual; Accounting and Billing Manual Section 3.2.1
stackable_with: Applies to all Aggregation market participation (Energy, AS, ICAP)

program_name: Energy Storage Resource (ESR) in an Aggregation - retail-rate charging (Order 841)
incentive_structure: Charging energy purchased at the applicable retail rate rather than wholesale LBMP
event_limits: Aggregations containing withdrawal-capable DER (Energy Storage Resources) may withdraw energy at retail rates per FERC Order No. 841; the Aggregation must supply the LSE PTID of the relevant retail authority for settlement. An Aggregation may be a Single Resource Type Aggregation of only ESRs, or a heterogeneous DER Aggregation mixing ESR, Intermittent Power Resources and Demand Side Resources
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Section 7.2.8
stackable_with: Energy arbitrage + ICAP + Ancillary Services from the same ESR Aggregation

program_name: Behind-the-Meter Net Generation (BTM:NG) Resource - exclusion from DER model
incentive_structure: Participates as a BTM:NG Resource rather than as a DER; not eligible for the Aggregation model
event_limits: A BTM:NG Resource routinely serves its host load from an on-site generation source, which precludes it from the DER participation model. A BTM:NG Resource that converts to a DER must thereafter routinely serve its host load by withdrawing from the grid rather than from on-site generation
tariff_schedule: Aggregation Manual Section 4.3.3
stackable_with: Not stackable with the DER Aggregation model

program_name: Installed Capacity - Special Case Resources (ICAP-SCR)
incentive_structure: Monthly $/kW-month UCAP capacity payment from ICAP auctions plus per-event energy payment at LBMP with a daily Minimum Payment Nomination (strike price) guarantee
incentive_value_usd: Capacity: monthly UCAP price from the ICAP Spot Market Auction for the resource's Load Zone (see per-zone price rows). Energy: real-time zonal LBMP with a daily guarantee of Minimum Payment Nomination recovery and a guaranteed four-hour minimum payment period
event_limits: Minimum 100 kW load reduction in aggregate by Load Zone; mandatory performance for a minimum of four hours when NYISO calls a reliability event; day-ahead advisory plus 2-hour in-day notice; SCRs activated before EDRP resources; must demonstrate maximum capacity obligation in each Capability Period (test or event at least once every six months); all SCRs carry a 4-hour duration requirement and are accredited commensurate with other four-hour resources; event/test meter data due within 75 days; failure to respond derates the resource and reduces future UCAP payments
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Sections 5.12.11, 5.12.13.1; ICAP Manual Section 4.12; Emergency Demand Response Program Manual (Manual 7)
stackable_with: May enroll simultaneously in ONE reliability-based program (SCR or EDRP) and ONE economic-based program (DADRP or DSASP); SCR energy payments are netted against any concurrent DADRP/DSASP payments and only reduction above the DADRP/DSASP schedule earns SCR energy payment (EDRP Manual 5.4.2). NOT stackable with the DER and Aggregation participation model - a Resource cannot be both an SCR and a DER at the same time

program_name: Emergency Demand Response Program (EDRP)
incentive_structure: $/MWh energy-only payment for verified load reduction during a NYISO-called reliability event; no capacity payment
incentive_value_usd: Greater of the real-time zonal LBMP or $500/MWh, with a guaranteed four-hour minimum payment period
event_limits: Minimum 100 kW load reduction; participation in any event is VOLUNTARY and there are no non-performance penalties; 2-hour in-day event notice; EDRP resources are activated after SCR resources; hourly interval metering required; event meter data due within 75 days; no capacity payment
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Attachment G Section 22.10; Emergency Demand Response Program Manual (Manual 7) Sections 2.2, 4.3, 5.4.2
stackable_with: One reliability program (EDRP or SCR) may be combined with one economic program (DADRP or DSASP); EDRP energy payment is reduced by any concurrent DADRP/DSASP payment (EDRP Manual 5.4.2). NOT stackable with the DER and Aggregation participation model

program_name: Day-Ahead Demand Response Program (DADRP)
incentive_structure: $/MWh Day-Ahead LBMP for scheduled load reduction plus a daily Curtailment Initiation Cost guarantee
incentive_value_usd: Day-Ahead LBMP times the lesser of actual or Day-Ahead scheduled load reduction; plus Curtailment Initiation Cost paid on a daily basis where applicable
event_limits: Minimum 1 MW reduction in aggregate by Load Zone and LSE; offers must be at or above the Monthly Net Benefit Offer Floor (MNBT); accepted offers notified by 11:00 a.m. for the next day midnight-to-midnight; response is MANDATORY when scheduled and penalties may apply if scheduled curtailment does not physically occur; hourly interval metering; CBL baseline (highest five of last ten like days); economic schedule meter data due within 55 days; no capacity payment; no real-time schedule
tariff_schedule: Day-Ahead Demand Response Program Manual (Manual 5); Technical Bulletin 245 (MNBT)
stackable_with: One economic program (DADRP or DSASP) may be combined with one reliability program (SCR or EDRP). NOT stackable with the DER and Aggregation participation model

program_name: Demand Side Ancillary Services Program (DSASP)
incentive_structure: $/MWh marginal clearing price for the Operating Reserve or Regulation product scheduled; no energy payment for the underlying reduction
incentive_value_usd: Reserve or Regulation market clearing price by location and product
event_limits: Minimum 1 MW reduction in aggregate by Load Zone; minimum energy offer at the Monthly Net Benefit Offer Floor; mandatory performance when scheduled and penalties may apply; requires 6-second two-way telemetry plus a revenue-grade interval billing meter and an instantaneous total load meter; must respond to 5-minute RTD base points for Reserves and 6-second AGC base points for Regulation; only interruptible load may supply Spinning Reserve or Regulation - loads backed by a qualified Local Generator may only supply Non-Synchronized Reserves; real-time baseline (actual load just prior to the real-time schedule); no capacity payment
tariff_schedule: Ancillary Services Manual; Services Tariff Rate Schedules 3 and 4
stackable_with: One economic program (DSASP or DADRP) may be combined with one reliability program (SCR or EDRP). NOT stackable with the DER and Aggregation participation model

program_name: Targeted Demand Response Program (TDRP)
incentive_structure: Energy payment at the rate of whichever program (SCR or EDRP) the resource is enrolled in; no separate TDRP payment
event_limits: Effective July 1 2007. Con Edison may request NYISO to activate demand response for local reliability in specific sub-load pockets of Load Zone J (New York City). Only existing SCR and EDRP resources in those locations are eligible, and participation is VOLUNTARY for both. TDRP responses cannot set the real-time market price. CSPs with resources in sub-load pockets are notified through the standard EDRP advisory process
tariff_schedule: Emergency Demand Response Program Manual (Manual 7) Section 6
stackable_with: Layered on top of an existing SCR or EDRP enrollment; not a standalone enrollment

program_name: Small Customer Aggregation (SCR / EDRP)
incentive_structure: Same payment as the underlying SCR or EDRP enrollment; this is a measurement and verification accommodation, not a separate revenue stream
event_limits: Allows resources with an ACL below the DRIS minimum kW limit to be aggregated and to use alternative validation methods such as statistical sampling to claim performance on a portfolio basis, in lieu of individual interval meters. Available for EDRP and SCR resources only (not DADRP or DSASP). Program-level minimums still apply at the aggregation level
tariff_schedule: Emergency Demand Response Program Manual (Manual 7) Section 2.7
stackable_with: Underlying SCR or EDRP program rules apply

program_name: ICAP Spot Market Auction - New York City (Zone J / NYC Locality) UCAP price
incentive_structure: $/kW-month UCAP clearing price in the monthly ICAP Spot Market Auction; the price an SCR or a DER Aggregation with CRIS in Zone J receives per kW of UCAP sold
incentive_value_usd: Summer 2026 Capability Period: May $32.59, Jun $32.53, Jul $12.41, Aug $12.35, Sep $12.39 per kW-month. Winter 2025-26: Nov 2025 $6.44, Dec 2025 $6.41, Jan 2026 $6.25, Feb 2026 $6.25, Mar 2026 $6.24, Apr 2026 $6.26 per kW-month. Summer 2025 for comparison: May $14.96, Jun $15.93, Jul $15.93, Aug $15.86, Oct $15.57 per kW-month
event_limits: Prices are monthly UCAP clearing prices. Summer Capability Period runs May through October; Winter Capability Period runs November through April. May and June 2026 were record NYC prices driven by a Locational Capacity Requirement increase and near-zero excess (0.06% and 0.09% above requirement). Selling capacity requires CRIS; a DER of 2 MW or less can obtain CRIS without a deliverability study
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Section 5.14 (ICAP Spot Market Auction); ICAP Manual

program_name: ICAP Spot Market Auction - Long Island (Zone K / LI Locality) UCAP price
incentive_structure: $/kW-month UCAP clearing price in the monthly ICAP Spot Market Auction for the Long Island locality
incentive_value_usd: Summer 2026 Capability Period: May $11.11, Jun $11.70, Jul $10.46, Aug $10.13, Sep $10.13 per kW-month. Winter 2025-26: LI cleared at the NYCA price - Nov 2025 $1.80, Dec 2025 $3.65, Jan 2026 $3.73, Feb 2026 $3.74, Mar 2026 $2.64, Apr 2026 $1.82 per kW-month. Summer 2025: LI cleared at the NYCA price of $5.23-$6.04 per kW-month

tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Section 5.14 (ICAP Spot Market Auction); ICAP Manual
stackable_with: SCR program; DER and Aggregation participation model ICAP participation

program_name: ICAP Spot Market Auction - G-J Locality (Lower Hudson Valley + NYC) UCAP price
incentive_structure: $/kW-month UCAP clearing price in the monthly ICAP Spot Market Auction for the G-J Locality (Zones G through J)
incentive_value_usd: Summer 2026 Capability Period: May $7.92, Jun $7.87, Jul $4.14, Aug $4.53, Sep $5.97 per kW-month. Winter 2025-26: Nov 2025 $1.80, Dec 2025 $3.65, Jan 2026 $3.73, Feb 2026 $3.74, Mar 2026 $2.64, Apr 2026 $1.82 per kW-month. Summer 2025: May $5.23, Jun $5.46, Jul $5.47, Aug $6.04, Oct $5.86 per kW-month
event_limits: In every month observed (Nov 2025 through Sep 2026) the G-J Locality cleared at the same price as NYCA/Rest of State, meaning the G-J constraint was not binding separately. Zone J prices are set separately and are much higher. Summer Capability Period runs May through October
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Section 5.14 (ICAP Spot Market Auction); ICAP Manual
stackable_with: SCR program; DER and Aggregation participation model ICAP participation

program_name: ICAP Spot Market Auction - NYCA / Rest of State (upstate) UCAP price
incentive_structure: $/kW-month UCAP clearing price in the monthly ICAP Spot Market Auction for the NYCA-wide (Rest of State) market
incentive_value_usd: Summer 2026 Capability Period: May $7.92, Jun $7.87, Jul $4.14, Aug $4.53, Sep $5.97 per kW-month (ROS price paid by LSEs, weighted average, equals the NYCA price in each of these months). Winter 2025-26: Nov 2025 $1.80, Dec 2025 $3.65, Jan 2026 $3.73, Feb 2026 $3.74, Mar 2026 $2.64, Apr 2026 $1.82 per kW-month. Summer 2025: May $5.23, Jun $5.46, Jul $5.47, Aug $6.04, Oct $5.86 per kW-month
event_limits: Upstate/Rest-of-State capacity is worth roughly one quarter to one fifth of New York City capacity in the Summer 2026 Capability Period. Summer Capability Period runs May through October; Winter runs November through April. Monthly auction; UCAP not ICAP
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Section 5.14 (ICAP Spot Market Auction); ICAP Manual
stackable_with: SCR program; DER and Aggregation participation model ICAP participation

program_name: ICAP market - Strip and Monthly (Capability Period) Auctions
incentive_structure: $/kW-month UCAP price from the Capability Period Auction (strip) or the Monthly Auction, as an alternative or supplement to the Spot Market Auction
event_limits: Aggregations and SCRs may offer into the Strip (Capability Period) Auction, the Monthly Auction, and the ICAP Spot Market Auction, or sell capacity bilaterally. Unsold UCAP is automatically offered into the Spot Market Auction
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Section 5.14; ICAP Manual Section 4; Aggregation Manual Section 2.2.5
stackable_with: SCR program; DER Aggregation ICAP participation; bilateral capacity contracts

program_name: FERC Order 2222 implementation status - DER Participation Model
incentive_structure: Rule / timeline row - no direct payment
event_limits: Timeline: NYISO filed its Aggregation participation model June 27 2019 (Docket ER19-2276); FERC accepted it January 23 2020 (170 FERC 61033). NYISO filed its Order 2222 compliance filing July 19 2021; FERC accepted it June 17 2022 while directing 30+ further tariff modifications. FERC granted NYISO an extension to December 31 2026 to complete full Order 2222 compliance. NYISO filed further DER tariff revisions June 1 2023 (Docket ER23-2040); FERC accepted them April 15 2024 (187 FERC 61022) and expressly found the 10 kW minimum capability requirement just and reasonable and NOT a temporary measure, while directing an informational report which NYISO filed April 15 2026. The DER and Aggregation participation model is LIVE today under the interim (pre-Order-2222) rules; dual-participation, operating-reserve composition and other rules change when the Order 2222-compliant tariff takes effect
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Sections 4.1.10 through 4.1.10.7.3; FERC Docket Nos. ER19-2276, ER21-2460, ER23-2040
stackable_with: Interim rules apply until the Order 2222-compliant tariff is implemented (targeted end of 2026)

program_name: Small Utility opt-in gate for DER Aggregation participation
incentive_structure: Eligibility gate - no payment
event_limits: New York has NO statewide opt-out of third-party aggregation of retail customers. The only gate is the Order 2222 small-utility provision: a Resource that is a customer of a Small Utility may not be enrolled in an Aggregation unless the Relevant Electric Retail Regulatory Authority affirmatively authorizes (opts in to) such participation. NYISO defines Small Utility as a Distribution Utility that distributed four million MWh or less in NYISO's immediately prior completed fiscal year (Jan 1 - Dec 31). The determination applies for the forthcoming Capability Year. If a RERRA later withdraws authorization and the Aggregator notifies NYISO before April 1, the DER is ineligible from the first day of the following Capability Year; if notice comes on or after April 1 but before May 1, the DER is ineligible as of June 1
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Section 4.1.10 (definitions of Distribution Utility and Small Utility)
stackable_with: Customers of New York's large investor-owned distribution utilities (over 4 million MWh/yr) face no opt-in gate and may join an Aggregation directly

program_name: Prohibition on duplicative compensation - same service in wholesale and retail
incentive_structure: Stacking gate - no payment
event_limits: A DER may not provide the SAME service in the NYISO-administered markets that it already provides in a retail service or program. FERC struck NYISO's originally proposed broader phrase or substantially similar as an improperly broad restriction, so the bar is same service only. The Aggregator must attest at enrollment that DER enrolled in its Aggregation are not providing the same service in a retail service or program, and must attest to compliance with the Distribution Utilities' tariffs and the RERRA's rules
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Sections 4.1.10.5 and 4.1.10.6
stackable_with: Different services (e.g. NYISO energy plus a retail locational or environmental credit) may be stacked; identical services may not

program_name: Stacking NYISO DER Aggregation with NY retail VDER Value Stack
incentive_structure: Retail VDER credits stacked on top of NYISO wholesale revenue
event_limits: Per the NY Joint Utilities DERA Duplicative Compensation Matrix (June 30 2025): VDER Energy and Capacity components are Utility Only and CANNOT be stacked with NYISO DERA. VDER Environmental Value (REC), Demand Reduction Value (DRV), Locational System Relief Value (LSRV), Market Transition Credit, Community Credit and Non-Mass Market Community Credit ARE stackable with a NYISO DER Aggregation. For storage, DRV, LSRV, MTC and Non-Mass Market Community Credit are stackable. Net Energy Metering is Utility Only and NOT stackable. Customers taking service under a utility Buyback Tariff are not eligible to participate in the NYISO DER aggregation model per tariff. Applicable retail tariffs are WVS and WDS (import and export) for storage; WDS tariffs are not yet approved or filed at FERC for all utilities
tariff_schedule: NY PSC VDER Value Stack; utility WVS and WDS tariffs; NYISO Services Tariff 4.1.10.6
export_compensation: VDER Value Stack energy and capacity components are forfeited if the DER sells energy or capacity into NYISO through an Aggregation
stackable_with: VDER DRV; VDER LSRV; VDER Environmental Value/REC; VDER Market Transition Credit; VDER Community Credit; Non-Wires Alternative contracts

program_name: Stacking NYISO DER Aggregation with utility demand response programs (CSRP / DLRP / DLM)
incentive_structure: Utility DR capacity and energy payments stacked on top of NYISO wholesale revenue
event_limits: Per the NY Joint Utilities DERA Duplicative Compensation Matrix (June 30 2025): utility Demand Response Program CAPACITY payments are stackable with a NYISO DER Aggregation for Demand Reduction, Generator and Energy Storage resource types. Utility Demand Response Program ENERGY payments are stackable but the resource is ineligible for the utility performance payment in hours with overlapping NYISO energy payments. Non-Wires Alternative contracts are stackable for all resource types including Landfill Gas. Separately, NYISO's own DR programs (SCR and EDRP) are marked fully stackable with utility DR programs during NYISO's interim market
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Section 4.1.11 (dual participation notice); NY Joint Utilities DERA Duplicative Compensation Matrix
stackable_with: Con Edison CSRP; Con Edison DLRP; Joint Utilities Dynamic Load Management; utility Non-Wires Alternative contracts

program_name: DER Aggregation - eligibility sizing rules (10 kW DER / 100 kW Aggregation / 20 MW injection cap)
incentive_structure: Eligibility gate - no payment
event_limits: Minimum capability of each individual DER (including a Demand Side Resource) participating in an Aggregation is 10 kW; where a DER includes multiple assets of different technologies at the facility, EACH asset must independently meet 10 kW. Minimum size of a DER Aggregation is 100 kW; an Aggregation that offers a combination of Energy injections, Energy withdrawals and/or Demand Reduction must be able to offer at least 100 kW of each. Maximum Injection Limit for an injecting facility in an Aggregation is 20 MW; there is no size cap on Demand Reduction resources. All DER in an Aggregation must be on the SAME Transmission Node and therefore in the same NYISO Load Zone. A DER facility has a single point of interconnection and a single utility account number, and may participate in only one Aggregation at a time. FERC found the 10 kW minimum just and reasonable on April 15 2024 and confirmed it is not a temporary measure
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Sections 4.1.10 and 4.1.10.1; NYISO Manual 38 (Aggregation Manual)
stackable_with: Resources under 10 kW remain eligible for EDRP, the SCR program (including Small Customer Aggregation) and NY State and utility DER programs

program_name: Energy Storage Resource (ESR) and Limited Energy Storage Resource (LESR) participation models
incentive_structure: Full participation in Energy, Ancillary Services and Installed Capacity markets as a standalone ESR, or as a Single Resource Type Aggregation of ESRs
event_limits: NYISO was the first ISO/RTO to allow full ESR participation in energy, capacity and ancillary services markets, implemented under FERC Order No. 841 (FERC accepted NYISO's Order 841 compliance revisions December 20 2019; full-participation model went live in 2020). Minimum size for wholesale participation as an ESR is 100 kW. A Limited Energy Storage Resource (LESR) is a regulation-focused model and must bid ISO-Committed-Flexible; an ESR may bid ISO-Committed-Flexible or Self-Committed Fixed/Flexible. Capacity market eligibility extends to resources able to store as little as two hours of energy, with time-stacking applied to resources with an Energy Duration Limitation (EDL). ESRs may withdraw (charge) at retail rates under Services Tariff 7.2.8
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Sections 7.2.8 and 15.4.1.2.4; ICAP Manual Attachment J; NYISO Manual 38 (Aggregation Manual) Section 2.1.3
export_compensation: Injections settled at Transmission Node LBMP; charging may be at wholesale LBMP or at the applicable retail rate
stackable_with: Energy arbitrage + Regulation + Operating Reserves + ICAP from the same ESR; ESR-only Single Resource Type Aggregation; heterogeneous DER Aggregation with solar and demand response

program_name: Regulation Service (Regulation Capacity and Regulation Movement)
incentive_structure: $/MWh Regulation Capacity clearing price plus $/MW Regulation Movement payment for AGC following
event_limits: Reachable by a BTM resource two ways: (1) as a Demand Side Resource in the DSASP program (minimum 1 MW in aggregate by Load Zone; only interruptible load qualifies for Regulation - load backed by a Local Generator does not); or (2) inside a NYISO Aggregation, where under current pre-Order-2222 rules EVERY individual DER in the Aggregation must itself be capable of providing Regulation, and the Aggregation must bid self-committed flexible. Requires 6-second AGC base point following and 6-second two-way telemetry. A Limited Energy Storage Resource (LESR) is the regulation-oriented storage model and bids ISO-Committed-Flexible. Clearing prices not captured here - see NYISO Ancillary Services market data
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Rate Schedule 3 and Section 15.4.1.2.4; Ancillary Services Manual; NYISO Manual 38 (Aggregation Manual) Section 2.2.4
stackable_with: Regulation + Energy + ICAP from the same resource; DSASP may be combined with SCR or EDRP but SCR/EDRP energy payments are netted against DSASP payments

program_name: Operating Reserves (10-Minute Spinning, 10-Minute Non-Synchronized, 30-Minute Synchronized, 30-Minute Non-Synchronized)
incentive_structure: $/MWh marginal clearing price by product and by reserve region
event_limits: Four Operating Reserve products. Reachable by a BTM resource via DSASP (minimum 1 MW in aggregate by Load Zone; only interruptible load may supply Spinning Reserve, while load served by a qualified Local Generator may supply Non-Synchronized Reserves) or via an Aggregation. Under current rules an Aggregation may only offer the product that EVERY member DER can supply - an aggregation of one 10-minute-spin facility plus two 30-minute-non-sync facilities can only offer 30-minute non-synchronized reserve. Aggregations must bid self-committed flexible; self-committed fixed and ISO-committed fixed bid modes are ineligible for reserves. New reserve Aggregations verify performance during the first two weeks of the first active month instead of prequalifying. DSASP resources must follow 5-minute RTD base points. Reserve prices differ by region (NYCA, East, SENY, Long Island); clearing prices not captured here
tariff_schedule: Services Tariff Rate Schedule 4 and Section 15.4.1.2.4; Ancillary Services Manual Section 6.12.2; NYISO Manual 38 (Aggregation Manual) Section 2.2.4
stackable_with: Reserves + Energy + ICAP from the same Aggregation; the all-members-capable restriction is scheduled to change under NYISO's Order 2222 implementation

program_name: Capacity Accreditation Factors (CAF) and Peak Load Window - 2025/2026 Capability Year
incentive_structure: Derating multiplier applied to ICAP before UCAP is sold; UCAP = ICAP x CAF x derating factor

program_name: Monthly Net Benefit Threshold (MNBT) - Order 745 net benefits test
incentive_structure: Price floor that gates energy payments for Demand Reductions
event_limits: NYISO runs the Net Benefits Test monthly and posts the Monthly Net Benefit Threshold by the 15th of the preceding month on its Demand Response page. A DER Aggregation or DADRP resource may OFFER below the MNBT, but Demand Reductions performed in an interval where the applicable Transmission Node LBMP is below the MNBT earn no Energy payment, no Day-Ahead Margin Assurance Payment and no Bid Production Cost Guarantee. Exception: if NYISO or the Transmission Owner dispatches the Aggregation for NYCA or local system reliability, the Demand Reductions remain eligible. A DER Aggregation also may not balance Energy withdrawals by Withdrawal-Eligible Generators against Demand Reductions in a Real-Time interval when the Transmission Node LBMP is below the MNBT. Current monthly values not captured here - they change every month

program_name: Co-located Storage Resource (CSR) participation model
incentive_structure: Energy, ancillary services and ICAP revenue for a storage resource sharing a point of injection with a co-located wind or solar resource
event_limits: FERC accepted NYISO's Co-located Storage Resource participation model on March 30 2021, covering Energy and Ancillary Services market rules, metering rules, the Interconnection Process, ICAP market participation rules and market power mitigation, for an ESR that shares a common point of injection with a wind or solar resource. Distinct from the Aggregation model - within an Aggregation, a facility with two or more technology types behind a single point of interconnection is treated as one DER with a maximum Injection Limit of 20 MW

program_name: SCR to DER Participation Model transition rules
incentive_structure: No payment - switching rule between the two capacity-earning DR pathways
event_limits: An active SCR may move to the DER participation model monthly: the SCR must be separated in DRIS before the close of the Certification period for the auction month preceding the intended first DER month. A transitioning SCR may use a Provisional DMNC capped at the upper limit of Installed Capacity calculated for the SCR (its former Average Coincident Load) for the immediately prior like Capability Period, submitted within the first 7 days of the pending-review month; the Provisional DMNC must later be validated by an in-period DMNC test and the Aggregation is exposed to oversold-capacity penalties. Moving the other way is much slower: a DER whose capability contributed to an Aggregation's UCAP must give notice by August 1 and can only rejoin the SCR program the following May 1. An SCR base performance test cannot substitute for a DMNC test. As of June 2025 the MMU reported only ONE demand response resource had actually transitioned from SCR to DER
